subject: BU-level GL mapping / net terms exception request (PO + invoice cadence)
messages:
From: Elena Ramos <elena.ramos@starlighthealth.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>
Cc: starlight.finance@starlighthealth.com, Tom Liu <tom.liu@starlighthealth.com>
Date: Tue, 20 Oct 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: BU GL codes, PO template and net terms exception

Hi Naomi,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the team is excited about Redwood's latency profile. Before legal/finance can issue a PO we need to confirm a couple of procurement constraints from our side:

- Our ERP requires line-level GL mapping tied to Business Unit codes on every invoice (we provided the template attached). Each invoice must include the BU code in the PO line description so our AP can auto-apply charges to the correct cost center.
- Standard net90 is our org default for new vendors, but Finance will only sign off on net60 if we receive a 12-month committed spend schedule (we can provide a commitment worksheet).
- Starlight prefers monthly invoices with a single consolidated PO per quarter (so we pass the quarterly PO to AP), but we sometimes need intra-quarter split invoices for multi-bu chargebacks.

Can Redwood accommodate: (a) visible BU/GL fields on the invoice line items, (b) acceptance of a quarterly PO plus the ability to split invoices against that PO by BU, and (c) a net60 exception in exchange for a 12-month commitment and a modest annual prepay? I've attached our PO template and GL mapping workbook.

Appreciate any details you can share; copying Tom from our ERP team in case you want to sync on technical formatting.

Best,
Elena Ramos
Senior Procurement Manager, Starlight Health
elena.ramos@starlighthealth.com
+1 312-555-0183

Attachments: Starlight_PO_Template_v3.pdf (PDF, 132KB); Starlight-ERP-GL-mapping.xlsx (XLSX, 48KB); Starlight_W9.pdf (PDF, 98KB)

From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Ramos <elena.ramos@starlighthealth.com>
Cc: ben.carter@redwood.ai, vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 20 Oct 2026 11:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: BU GL codes, PO template and net terms exception

Hi Elena — thanks for the detail and for the attachments, this is very clear. Short answers up front:

- Invoice line-level GL/BU field: yes. Our billing supports an extra free-text field at the line level (we commonly expose it as "cost_center" or "BU code") which we can populate from the PO line description. We also support a CSV-friendly billing export your ERP can ingest.
- Quarterly PO + split invoices: we can accept a single master PO number for the quarter and issue multiple invoices that reference the master PO and include the specific BU code on each line for your AP to split internally.
- Net terms: our standard public terms are net30, but for enterprise we've accepted net45/60 in exceptional cases tied to contractual commitments. Net60 against a 12-month commit is something I can escalate — we will likely need a short addendum (payment schedule + SOW/commitment appendix).

Two asks from our side to keep this moving smoothly:
1) Can Tom share a sample flat file layout your AP expects (column names for GL code, BU, PO, invoice_line_id, amount)? If you prefer we can map to a small sample export and validate in a short call.
2) For the net60 ask: can you confirm the expected cadence of the 12-month commitment (monthly invoice amounts vs. quarterly forecast)? That will determine how our finance team models the credit exposure.

I'll loop in Ben and Vanessa from Sales/Finance to coordinate commercial tradeoffs. If it's helpful we can set a 30-minute technical sync with your ERP lead + our billing engineer.

Thanks,
Naomi
Sr. Sales Operations, Redwood Inference
naomi.feldman@redwood.ai

Naomi / Vanessa — quick internal notes on the commercial side after reviewing Elena's ask:

- Net60 in exchange for a 12-month commitment is reasonable for mid-size health systems. We should consider: small reduction in list price (we can offer a 5% contract-level discount) or a one-time onboarding credit to offset collection risk.
- Accepting quarterly PO + split invoices is functionally fine but higher operational overhead vs. straight monthly invoicing. Recommend we ask for: (a) the master PO number structure, and (b) a sample flat file to validate automation so we don't create manual work for Billing.
- If Finance requires additional comfort, we can propose an early-payment option: Starlight can prepay 2 months up front for a 6% discount and get net60 for the remainder.

My call to action: Naomi, if you agree I'll propose the following options to Elena:
1) Net60 with 12-month commit + no price change but 30-day onboarding holdback (release after first invoice paid)
2) Net60 with 12-month commit + 5% annual discount
3) Net30 standard (no commit)

Pick which options to present; I'll draft the language for the commercial addendum.

Thanks,
Ben
